name: Natioro
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Dyachkov, Vadim. 2021. When Gur class markers are absent: suffix omission in Natioro. Language in Africa 2(4). 26-44. doi:10.37892/2686-8946-2021-2-4-26-44
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online (also online with a university library login)
sources.note: Only a one-line phonological note in sec. 2 (p. 29): 'In Natioro, three tone levels (high, mid and low) are distinguished.' No word 'stress' or 'accent' anywhere; data (Timba dialect, own fieldwork 2018-2020) carry tone marks; mentions tonal overlays on nouns. States 'The only sources containing basic data on Natioro are Prost (1968) and Miehe & Winkelmann (2007).'

sources.citation: Heath, Jeffrey. 2026. A grammar of Paleni (Samic/Gur family, Burkina Faso). Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.21904854. 426 pp. [sister language Palen, pln]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: NOT Natioro. Sec. 3.1.2 (p. 13): 'Paleni does not have a discernible stress system. However, there are hints of a subtle prosodic organization into CvCv and Cvv units starting at the left edge of stems.' On Natioro it says only (p. 4) that the Samic family = Wara, Paleni, Natioro (Winkelmann 2007) and 'Natioro [is being studied] by Vadim Dyachkov'; no Natioro phonological data.

sources.citation: Dyachkov, V. V. 2022. Deverbal adjectives are different from regular participles: The case of Natioro (Gur). Acta Linguistica Petropolitana 18(3). 104-129. doi:10.30842/alp23065737183104129
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p. 107: 'Like most African languages, Natioro is a tonal language, with three tone levels (high, mid and low) distinguished.' Nothing on stress/accent; fieldwork 2018-2022, Timba dialect.

sources.citation: Dyachkov, V. V. 2021. Preposition à in Natioro: From comitatives to clausal conjunction. Acta Linguistica Petropolitana 17(1). 384-405. doi:10.30842/alp23065737171384405
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p. 387: 'Like most African languages, Natioro is a tonal language and has three tone levels (high, mid and low).' Also p. 387-388: nouns 'are subject to tonal overlays.. it is not clear whether these overlays can be analyzed as case markers or they are due to downdrift.' No mention of stress/accent.

sources.citation: Sawadogo, Tasséré. 2002. Rapport d'enquête sur le natioro. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2003-005. 42 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sociolinguistic survey (villages, bilingualism in Jula, SRT testing) with a phonetic wordlist from 7 villages (Kawara, Timba, Dinaoro, Niansogoni, Negeni, Sourani, Faniagara) 'conformes aux normes de l'AIP' (p. 42); no statement on tone, accent or stress. Sec. 1.9 'Travaux linguistiques' names only Prost 1968 and an unpublished SIL 1982 survey (Groff & Solomiac). Obtained via the Internet Archive.archive.org because sil.org is could not be reached by automated download.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page for nati1243 and Grambank page nati1243
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Glottolog lists Prost 1968 (grammar sketch) and Tauxier 1939 (wordlist) as descriptive sources; 'Comments on subclassification' cite Winkelmann 2007. Grambank coded Natioro from Prost 1968 only. No stress information.

sources.citation: Prost, André. 1968. Notes sur le Natioro. In Deux langues voltaïques en voie de disparition: le wara et le natioro (Documents linguistiques 14), 39-79. Dakar: Université de Dakar.

sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number Philol 893 vol.14
sources.note: Only pre-2021 grammar sketch of Natioro (41 pp., French); Prost's Voltaic sketches normally open with a 'Phonétique' section covering tons and accent; Dyachkov and Sawadogo both name it as the sole basic description. Harvard print copy (Widener Library (offsite storage) Philol 893 vol.14) is(a scan can be requested through your own library).

sources.note: Second of the two sources Dyachkov says contain basic Natioro data; chapters in this series give phonological preliminaries (tone, syllable) for each language from 1992 field notebooks (Winkelmann/Kleinewillinghöfer). Print only; publisher site now defunct.

sources.citation: Groff, Randall & Solomiac, Paul. 1982. Rapport d'enquête linguistique sur les wara et les natioro. ms., SIL Burkina Faso archives, Ouagadougou.

sources.note: Unpublished SIL survey with Faniagara/Negeni wordlists reused by Sawadogo 2002; survey-level, unlikely to state stress but is the only other primary Natioro data before 2018.

sources.citation: Winkelmann, Kerstin. 2007. K4 Samu group: Comparative notes. In Miehe, Gudrun & Winkelmann, Kerstin (eds.), Noun class systems in Gur languages, Vol. I: Southwestern Gur languages (without Gurunsi) (Gur Monographs 9), 561-565. Köln: Rüdiger Köppe.
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.note: This is the 'Winkelmann 2007' the earlier scan named: Glottolog ref 302243, a 5-page comparative noun-class note on the Samu group (listed by Glottolog as an overview;comparative), not a Natioro description. The same volume (Köppe, print only; publisher site now defunct) is cited by Dyachkov as one of the two sources with basic Natioro data; Heath 2026 lists its K3 chapter on Paleni (Kleinewillinghöfer, 541-560), so a K1/K2 Natioro chapter is likely but unverified. Not online.
